title: Three publication specimens, one caller contract

ch8-session.label: CHIP-8 normalized events, frames, and native evidence

pico-session.label: PICO-8 normalized events, frames, and native evidence

pico-readme.label: PICO-8 supported subset and runtime qualification

tic-session.label: TIC-80 normalized events, frames, and native evidence

tic-readme.label: TIC-80 supported subset and runtime qualification

chip8.text: Raw bytes loaded at 0x200; 1–63,488 bytes; CHIP-8/SCHIP/XO-CHIP variants are selected through configuration.

pico8.text: Cartridge extension accepts text .p8, steganographic .p8.png, and .p8.rom forms; 1 byte–4 MiB.

tic80.text: Binary .tic cartridge artifact; 1 byte–16 MiB; Lua is the implemented runtime.

chip8.text: Instruction-stepped virtual machine with 64 KiB address space and timer/frame ticks; instruction schema is word16.

pico8.text: Bounded Lua compatibility runtime invokes cartridge callbacks; the exposed instruction schema is a Lua operation, not an instruction-exact PICO-8 trace.

tic80.text: Bounded Lua compatibility runtime invokes BOOT/TIC callbacks; the exposed instruction schema is a Lua operation, not an instruction-exact TIC-80 trace.

chip8.text: Schema chip8.machine_configuration@2: quirk preset (default chip8), instructions per hardware frame (default 12), machine seed (default 0).

pico8.text: Schema pico8.machine_configuration@1: one callback per frame (fixed at 1), per-callback Lua instruction budget, machine seed (default 0).

tic80.text: Schema tic80.machine_configuration@1: one callback per frame (fixed at 1), Lua runtime only, machine seed (default 0).

chip8.text: Sixteen separately identified hexadecimal keys; typed key values, scheduled or live delivery, frame-start coordinate.

pico8.text: Sixteen separately identified buttons; scheduled frame-start delivery; digital-key family enables selective value evidence.

tic80.text: One scheduled frame-start gamepad input carrying an unsigned 32-bit button mask; no live delivery advertised.

chip8.text: Hardware frame boundary at 60 Hz; step coordinate counts instructions. Configurable instructions/frame change machine progression.

pico8.text: Callback boundary defines a semantic frame; step coordinate is a tick. The callback is the bundle’s frame unit, not a claim of exact upstream timing.

tic80.text: Callback boundary defines a semantic frame; step coordinate is a tick. One callback per frame; no instruction-level trace claim.

chip8.text: 128×64 physical backing pixels in plane-major form; hash and full artifact schemas. Low-resolution modes are represented on the backing surface.

pico8.text: 128×128 palette-index bytes; separate fingerprint and full-frame schemas.

tic80.text: 240×136 RGBA8 pixels; separate SHA-256 fingerprint and full-frame schemas.

chip8.text: Execution lifecycle, frame, instruction, branch/call/return, memory/register/stack/display, input, timer/sound, and trap events.

pico8.text: Lifecycle, frame-completed, input-applied, halt/crash events; no per-Lua-operation stream is promised.

tic80.text: Lifecycle, frame, input-applied/sampled, and TIC-80 trace-extension events; trace granularity is bundle-defined, not per Lua instruction.

chip8.text: Typed chip8.event evidence includes display/draw, control transfer, key wait/sample, timer, memory, stack, and invalid-opcode facts.

pico8.text: Versioned native events for frame completion, accepted input, runtime errors, and execution summary.

tic80.text: Versioned native events for frame completion, accepted/sampled gamepad input, TIC trace records, and execution summary.

chip8.text: Session snapshot schema chip8.session.snapshot@5; snapshot captures resumable state, not frame history.

pico8.text: State-only session snapshot pico8.state.session_snapshot@2; continuation does not depend on retained frame history.

tic80.text: State-only session snapshot tic80.state.session_snapshot@2; continuation does not depend on retained frame history.

chip8.text: Native-backed framebuffer, execution summary, interestingness, coverage, trajectory identity; bounded control-flow, visual-trajectory, and input-summary reducers.

pico8.text: Native-backed execution summary; bounded visual-motif and input-summary reducers over declared frame/event or selected input evidence.

tic80.text: Native-backed execution summary; bounded visual-motif and input-summary reducers over declared frame/event or selected gamepad evidence.

chip8.text: Optional static analyzer and verifier inspect CHIP-8 instruction/program structure and machine-specific validity.

pico8.text: Optional static analyzer and verifier report cartridge/Lua structure and the explicitly supported PICO-8 compatibility subset.

tic80.text: Optional static analyzer and verifier inspect cartridge chunks, Lua language selection, and callback structure for the implemented subset.

chip8.text: glassvm-chip8; entry point chip8; import module glassvm_chip8; Python ≥3.12; glassvm.python_bundle protocol 1.0.0.

pico8.text: glassvm-pico8; entry point pico8; import module glassvm_pico8; Python ≥3.12; glassvm.python_bundle protocol 1.0.0.

tic80.text: glassvm-tic80; entry point tic80; import module glassvm_tic80; Python ≥3.12; glassvm.python_bundle protocol 1.0.0.

shared_contract.text: All three use the same caller-owned request and preparation boundary: artifact, typed configuration, input schedule, execution controls, and observation are resolved before execution; PreparedRun remains separate from PreparedObservation. The shared FileRunSession owns sink assembly, execution/evidence accounting, recorder finalization, and atomic publication. Machine-specific schemas, timing, event semantics, and supported subsets remain bundle-owned.

scope_note: CHIP-8 is the baseline/reference implementation. PICO-8 and TIC-80 are external publication-validation specimens, not complete or instruction-exact emulators. Both use bounded Lua 5.4 compatibility runtimes; upstream PICO-8 semantics are not claimed as exact, and upstream TIC-80 targets Lua 5.3. Claims are limited to the documented and tested subsets.
